x: Don MacLean had been given the first leg to Wandsworth Common and the first stroke of ten o'clock sent him on his way with nineteen other runners.

Don Maclean who is in great form these days, went off last and with a good effort gained one place to bring us into fifth place. With a fit team we could have done better but in the circumstances the team ran well.

Clive Shippen, now almost fit again, held fifth place without losing ground on Woodford and handed over to Don Maclean for the final leg fifty seconds down on T.V.H. and thirty-three down on Woodford Green A.C.

Don Maclean (17.55) Don was given this stage as a result of his fine last-leg efforts in the Poly and Surrey Road Relays. Although the task on this occasion was far more difficult as Woodford and Walton were 95 and 82 secs ahead, respectivly; the latter setting fastest time of the day.
Gordon was well backed up by Shipley (3rd), Maclean & Shippen (6th), Forey (8th) and Miller (12th).
Maclean, who had not had a happy winter season, showed how much better he performs over the shorter distances by recording 14.53 for the 'B' team.
Kerr, Newell, Davies, Walker, Black, Dabbs, Linstead, Maclean. How's that for a line up to set a new 3 mile record?
Our "B", "C", and "D" teams also produced some good performances notably from Maclean, Sawyer and Forey, and all but the "C" team closed in.
O'Hara and Maclean finished first and second in the mile with two youngsters Fairclough and Bicourt fighting it out for fourth and fifth places to clock 4:31.0 and 4:32.0 respectively.

Jones, 109th Maclean, 115th Morrison, 138th Hampshire, 144th D.W. Jones, 148th Paget, 170th Angus, 195th Forey, 208th Piddington, 229th Penny,257th Conway, 267th Pepe, 276th Henn, 305th Fairfield, 306th Satchell, 324th Smithers, 327th D.

Yet during our recent lean years, the name of Pat Newell has figured consistently and he has, along with other stalwarts like Walker, Linstead, Dabbs, Davies and Maclean, Helped keep the Belgrave flag flying, albeit a little limply.
In spite of a strong headwind on the outward leg of the journey, 5k came up in 14:55 with Mays (Kent AC), Wardle (London Irish), Maclean (Team Southampton) and Phil Wicks making up the leading bunch.

In the red vest with white/red shorts towards the left is the eventual race winner Angus Maclean (Team Southampton). 31 is Richard Ward (Belgrave/Surrey), 32 Phil Wicks (Belgrave/Surrey), between and just behind these latter two is Tim Watson in a white/green vest (Belgrave/Hampshire).
